scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom has been hosting Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for about 50 years, and now she's too old, so we, her four kids, are supposed to take over by rotating. Each of us has hosted one holiday so far. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family has never been close, and they live all over the country. This year, her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. At first, it was just a sister trip, but then they invited all their kids and grandkids to meet them there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event, and I agree with that. Plus, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably have to end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York and went on about how sad Mom will be that I'm doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions and also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that me and him could maybe just swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I'm trying to spend Thanksgiving with my wife's family, which is a big deal for us, especially since it's a once-in-a-lifetime event. On the other hand, I'm breaking the tradition that our mom worked hard to maintain, and I'm making it difficult for my siblings to handle the hosting responsibilities. I wonder if it's more important to stick to the family tradition or to prioritize my own family's wishes. Is it fair to my siblings to change the plan at the last minute? Did I handle the situation well by offering solutions and trying to swap with my brother? Or should I have just stuck to the original plan and hosted Thanksgiving as agreed? I also think about how our mom would feel. She's the one who started this tradition, and she's probably counting on us to keep it going. By not hosting, am I letting her down? And what about the precedent this sets for future Thanksgivings? If I break the rotation this year, will it cause more problems in the future? I'm also considering the feelings of my wife and daughter. They're really excited about this opportunity, and it's important to them. Should family traditions always come before individual family wishes? Or is it okay to make exceptions in certain cases? I'm feeling torn between honoring the family tradition and supporting my own family's desires. I want to do the right thing, but I'm not sure what that is in this situation. Maybe I should talk to my siblings again and see if there's a way to compromise or find a middle ground. Or perhaps I need to accept that sometimes traditions have to change to accommodate new circumstances. Overall, I'm not sure if I'm in the wrong or not. I need to weigh the importance of family traditions against the happiness of my own family and see where the balance lies.
